$comment: Estate host profiles — where prime-silo's services live, selectable per machine. Pick one with ESTATE_HOST=<name> (or the 'active' field). config.mjs uses the chosen profile's values as DEFAULTS; an explicit env var (BENNY_API_HOST, BENNY_LMSTUDIO_ENDPOINTS, NEO4J_URI, BENNY_HOME, LONGVIEW_WORKSPACE, BENNY_EMBED_*) always wins. This is the 'configurable as in the estate' seam: move compute between the T480 and the ASUS by changing ESTATE_HOST, not by hand-editing endpoints.
$rules: workspace_root (cards/data_out/ledger) MAY live on OneDrive so every machine shares one corpus (OneDrive = primary/SoR).

neo4j_data_dir MUST stay LOCAL per machine — a live graph DB on OneDrive sync corrupts. The graph rebuilds deterministically from the shared cards (model→graph), so nothing is lost by keeping it local.
portable F: snapshots stay passive backups (estate_backup.mjs), not the operational store.

t480.note: 16 GB RAM — tight when LM Studio (gemma+embedder) + Neo4j + benny run together; prefer offloading heavy runs to the ASUS.

asus.role: satellite / compute — runs prime-silo (pipeline + benny + Neo4j)
asus.note: The pipeline + benny + Neo4j run HERE. LM Studio + the nomic embedder stay on the T480, so lm_endpoint/embed_base point at the T480 (192.168.68.125:1234). Workspace comes from the shared OneDrive; Neo4j data stays LOCAL (neo4j_data_dir). bind_host 0.0.0.0 exposes benny to the LAN so the T480 hub can monitor/remote-control it. neo4j_data_dir defaults to %LOCALAPPDATA% (always local, always present); override with NEO4J_DATA_DIR to reuse a pre-built graph.
